meta.storyTitle: Reconcile daemon RPC registration and audit coverage

summary.prose: Keep Batch05's exact registration, audit, routing and documentation reconciliation. Correct the discovered authority gap in modifying RPC routes while preserving existing error/result shapes. For tools.call, preserve unknown-tool, schema, cancellation and approval-denial behavior, then enforce explicit registered-repository authority immediately before capability execution; the new refusal for an otherwise admitted operation is an intentional compatibility change requiring approval.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Reconcile daemon RPC registration and audit coverage

api.name: buildHandlerRuntime

parameters.name: deps
parameters.purpose: Existing runtime services; contract tests use inert stubs for construction and isolated daemon-owned stores for dispatch.

returns.meaning: Assembled rpcHandlers and streamHandlers, including spread registrations; these actual maps are the registration inventory.

preconditions: Construction-only checks must not execute provider calls or open the installed daemon's stores.
postconditions: RPC_AUDIT keys equal the union of constructed unary and stream registrations with no missing or stale entries. Each audit row has reviewed evidence and a valid kind; modifying rows alone carry their existing repository/path rules.
methodClasses entries uniquely cover every constructed method with the exact transport flag. Preserve an independently reviewed compatibility key inventory, updating only explained added methods.

Add daemon.qualificationState as read-only in the repo audit and unary session-class in methodClasses: it reads journal/release/graph metadata through the full handler runtime. It is not shared state, FIFO-exempt or an admin-board method. Session workers already load this runtime and enter daemon store and maintenance guards.

Retired review methods retain explicit main-daemon refusal ownership. Tests must verify membership in the named retired-review ownership sets and existing router precedence, rather than assume the entire codeReview family runs on shared-state workers.

Callable step phase contracts, including frozen inert review schemas, are the independent expected phase inventory. Include design-review-step.cancel as read-only with unavailability evidence and reconcile any additional missing/stale phases only against their actual callable dispatcher/schema. Never restore deleted review execution.
docs/daemon.md lists exactly FILE_MODIFYING_METHODS with the correct repo parameter and all six refusal codes. Remove retired-review modifying rows and document current modifying registrations.

Previously unaudited team.park/team.resume/team.settle are modifying repo-scoped operations; their new explicit repo refusals are intentional. repo.settings.set remains modifying but preserves its own exact-registration check and structured error envelope. tools.call is explicitly modifying, with its authority check placed at execution admission rather than generic stream entry.

preconditions: Method-class data remains worker-safe and imports no handler runtime.
postconditions: Keep existing admin/indexing and shared-state routing behavior. qualificationState is ordinary session work: nested calls stay inline on the current full-runtime daemon thread.
Explicitly test unknown, missing, stale, duplicate and wrong-transport inventory drift. Do not add family fallbacks or blanket reviewed exemptions.

Ownership relationships are metadata lookups: each registered key has one execution class and one audited repo-scope kind, while transport membership is checked independently. Existing main-thread overrides take priority over session class. No domain entity, module-dependency or public IPC shape changes require a new ERD or interaction diagram; these explicit ownership rules suffice.

api.name: executeTool
api.signature: executeTool(toolId: string, input: ToolInput, deps: ToolDeps): Promise<ToolResult>

parameters.name: deps
parameters.purpose: Existing daemon execution context; the tools.call adapter supplies an internal repository-authority check using the daemon registry, never a caller-supplied wire callback.

returns.meaning: Existing result shape, including unsuccessful results for earlier failures or denied repository authority.

preconditions: No duplicated executor validation or new executor framework. No new IPC fields or direct cloud REST.
postconditions: Preserve this order: tool lookup and existing temporary-session checks; existing input-schema rejection; cancellation; approval description and denial; final cancellation; repository authority for otherwise admitted tools.call; capability execution and successful hooks.
Unknown tool, invalid schema, cancelled call or declined approval must preserve its existing result/error and perform no repository registry lookup.

At final admission, an invalid/unregistered repo yields an unsuccessful ToolResult using the existing failure shape, with the existing repo refusal code in its error text; no capability execute or success hook runs.
Only the daemon installs the admission check for tools.call. Existing other executor callers retain their current contracts; no transport argument can supply a callback or waive authority.
For an admitted operation, canonicalize repoPath from the authority check before execution. Preserve stream done/error envelopes and existing successful tool result shape.

The new refusal for an otherwise admitted tools.call targeting an invalid repository is an intentional authority correction. Earlier blanket no-public-failure-change wording is superseded by these explicit ordering and compatibility rules.

errorCases.scenario: A new or merged method lacks an audit/class entry, or an old row is no longer registered.
errorCases.detection: Bidirectional exact key comparison against constructed unary and stream maps, plus callable phase inventory.
errorCases.response: Fail the named contract test with missing/stale keys; do not synthesize a default classification.
errorCases.userImpact: Prevents silently ungated mutation or requests sent to unsupported owners.

errorCases.scenario: Missing, relative, nonexistent, unregistered or mismatched repository, or path traversal outside it.
errorCases.detection: Existing requireRepoForCall and dispatch tests, including conflicting cwd/environment and continuation token cases.
errorCases.response: Retain the existing six refusal codes before repository mutation; stream refusal remains an error frame.
errorCases.userImpact: Caller gets the existing actionable refusal and repository files remain unchanged.

errorCases.scenario: Unavailable review called through RPC or a frozen step phase, including cancel.
errorCases.detection: Existing Batch04 unavailable-boundary and router precedence controls.
errorCases.response: Preserve the current unavailable response before repo lookup, worker allocation or review work.
errorCases.userImpact: Retired reviews remain unavailable and cause no writes or provider calls.

errorCases.scenario: qualificationState has no completed rollback, release identity mismatch, or missing/wrong graph fixture.
errorCases.detection: Existing handler guards and an isolated negative dispatch control.
errorCases.response: Keep the existing no-completed-qualification or missing-fixture error; never return fabricated success or route to an admin worker lacking the handler.

errorCases.scenario: tools.call is unknown, input-schema-invalid, cancelled or denied while its repoPath is invalid/unregistered.
errorCases.detection: Dedicated executor/stream regression controls with a repository checker spy that fails if called.
errorCases.response: Return the existing earlier executor result unchanged; never replace it with repository refusal.
errorCases.userImpact: Existing actionable failures retain their precedence and format.

errorCases.scenario: An otherwise admitted tools.call would execute in an invalid or unregistered repository.
errorCases.detection: Daemon-supplied final admission check after existing validation, cancellation and approval denial handling.
errorCases.response: Return an unsuccessful ToolResult in the existing done envelope, carrying the repo refusal code in error text; execute and success hooks are untouched.
errorCases.userImpact: Intentional new authority refusal; caller supplies a valid registered repo before retrying.

invariantsToPreserve.text: Repository authority derives from explicit registered canonical repo or an already-supported validated continuation token, never daemon environment/cwd.
Daemon-owned storage, worker-safe classification imports and existing main-thread refusal ownership remain intact.
Review implementation stays retired; frozen schemas remain inert compatibility data. Qualification evidence regeneration belongs to another batch.

migration.stateBefore: Task-one code and all mapped tests/typecheck pass, but two build validation attempts reject the tools.call authority ordering under the original blanket failure-preservation requirement. The current early callback is unfinished, unapproved build work.
migration.stateAfter: Exact inventories remain reconciled and final tool admission authority preserves earlier executor failures. Only otherwise admitted operations gain the explicitly approved repository refusal.

migrationSteps.action: Obtain human approval of this revised LLD and a replacement PLAN before continuing implementation. Replace the unfinished early tools.call callback with the approved final admission ordering; keep completed inventory/retired-router checks.
Reconcile documentation with reviewed modifying rules; run the complete affected files serially through the coordinator, retain evidence and update the failure/batch record.

Present validated BUILD for human approval before completion. Deployment/restart uses the normal separate daemon lifecycle; no installed daemon change or release qualification is required to validate this batch.

migration.backwardCompat: Public parameter/result schemas, storage formats and existing malformed/unknown/schema/cancellation/denial responses remain unchanged. Previously unaudited modifying team routes gain explicit repo refusal. Otherwise admitted tools.call operations with invalid/unregistered repos gain an intentional unsuccessful ToolResult before capability execution; registered successful operations keep their prior shape. No data rewrite or installed daemon restart is required.

alternativesConsidered.name: Authorize immediately before admitted tool execution
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Preserve earlier executor failures and enforce explicit repository authority before any admitted capability runs.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Retain explicit RPC/phase/class reconciliation and independent exact inventories. For tools.call, reuse the existing executor after unknown-tool, schema, cancellation and approval-denial handling; apply repository authority before capability execution and hooks. Define new repository refusals as an intentional compatibility change only for otherwise admitted operations.
pros: Preserves earlier actionable failures and existing transport/result shapes.
Closes the audited authority gap without duplicating executor validation.
cons: An otherwise admitted operation targeting an invalid/unregistered repository now fails intentionally; requires human design approval.

alternativesConsidered.name: Gate every tool request at the stream boundary
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Authorize before resolving and validating the selected capability.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Use the current generic modifying stream gate or the early toolsCall repository callback before executeTool. This is simple but changes unknown-tool, invalid schema, cancellation and denial precedence for requests with invalid repositories.
cons: Fails the required preservation of existing earlier executor errors and repeats the rejected build behavior.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Build validation rejected this ordering because it replaces existing executor failures before any capability could execute.
